category: Reservoirs, dams, levees, and flood-control operations for Western Washington basins
summary: Seattle District (NWS) reservoir data for Howard A. Hanson (HAH) and Mud Mountain (MMD) dams, Lake Washington Ship Canal (LWSC), and the Section 7 utility dams (Ross, Upper/Lower Baker, Diablo, Gorge, Chester Morse) IS machine-accessible, but not where the prompt assumed: the public CWMS Data API (cwms-data.usace.army.mil/cwms-data) returns zero time series for office=NWS; the same series are published under office=NWDP (Pacific Northwest Region, 27,826 series) and also via (a) the undocumented-but-working water.usace.army.mil/cda/reporting/providers/nws/... JSON/CSV endpoints, (b) the legacy NWD Dataquery 2.0 web service (getjson/ecsv; decommission date 'to be announced'), and (c) NOAA NWRFC xml.cgi / NWPS API (HHDW1, MMRW1, RODW1, UBDW1, DIAW1, MORW1, TLRW1). USGS NWIS carries hourly pool elevation/storage for HHD (12105800), MMD (12098000), Ross/Diablo/Gorge (12175000/12176500/12177700), Baker Lake/Lake Shannon (12191600/12193000), Chester Morse (12115900), SF Tolt Reservoir (12147900) and Lake Tapps plus its diversion/return (12101000, 12098920, 12101100). Regulation rules are documented in fetched water control manuals and USACE's 2013 Skagit hydrology report (HHD: 12,000 cfs control / 10,000 cfs rising target at Auburn, pools 1,141/1,167/1,206 ft; MMD: 106,000 ac-ft, 45,000 cfs target at Puyallup, 12,000 cfs White River secondary; Ross: 120,000 ac-ft by Dec 1 through Mar 15, Corps takes control when Concrete forecast exceeds 90,000 cfs; Upper Baker: 74,000 ac-ft Nov 15-Mar 1; no authorized flood storage at Lower Baker, Diablo or Gorge). The pending Skagit settlement (filed May 2026) would raise Ross storage to 140,000 ac-ft by Nov 1 with a 165,000 ac-ft buffer (secondary sources). NID (OpenAPI + 67 MB national CSV + ArcGIS FeatureServer, 835 WA records) and NLD (ArcGIS FeatureServer/MapServer + OGC WFS; 339 WA levee systems incl. Skagit Dike Districts 1/3/9/12/17/22, Green, Cedar, Puyallup, Nooksack, Snohomish) are fully machine-readable. The Nooksack has no major dams and is unregulated (NOAA 2025 EA). Ecology's dam inventory is report/Excel-only (Jan 2026 revision; scripted fetches blocked by WAF) with a 2017 GIS layer available by request. County flood warning systems are mostly web-only: King County's app API requires an Azure APIM subscription key; Skagit and Whatcom counties link to USGS/NWPS; Snohomish County's OneRain portal now redirects to a login.

providers.quality_flags: TSID version suffix encodes provenance: -RAW vs -REV (revised/screened), source tags (IRIDIUM, GOES, NWSRADIO, USGS-SNAPPED, SCL-RAW, PSE-RAW, CBT, RFC-FCST, CENWS-COMPUTED). Per-value quality-code integer.

providers.licensing: U.S. federal government data (public domain by default); API software MIT-licensed. No explicit data terms page found (OPEN_QUESTION). Provisional-data warnings apply on the NWD project pages.
